what: Wf-A111 (MOD4/T7) wire-in smoke for the decode-time ring prior, per the standing 50-step rule. Three flags are new: --ring-prior, --ring-prior-min-ring-size, --ring-prior-max-ring-size.

1_parse_args_accepts_the_flags.how: YAML round-trip: a copy of the smoke config with `ring_prior: true` and `ring_prior_min_ring_size: 5` under `flow:`, then parse_args() with --config only.

2_trainer_initialises_and_the_decoder_re.stdout_line: [cfm-decoder] decision=threshold @ threshold=0.500 (metrics and decode now share this rule) | connectivity_prior=on @ min_logit=0.000 (D2 postprocess, no retrain needed) | ring_prior=on @ min=5, max=None | dative_max_distance=2.60 A

5_the_prior_does_not_enter_the_objective.why: The prior is decode-time only. A flag that also reaches the loss would be the duplicate-loss-path defect; the check is that the training quantities are unchanged with the flag on.

wiring_effect_on_a_1_epoch_model.note: NOT a quality result. This model is one epoch old on 64 clouds and its geometry is a blob (single_fragment_ratio 0.000 in both arms). The numbers are here because they show the prior reaching the trainer's OWN per-epoch report (gen_ring_*), not because they say anything about generated chemistry.
wiring_effect_on_a_1_epoch_model.reading: On a blob the prior converts a triangle mesh into a pentagon mesh: the 5+6 share goes 0.057 -> 0.986 while single_fragment_ratio stays 0.000. The share reached the right value for the wrong reason, which is why the effect is measured on a trained checkpoint in wfa111_ring_prior_ab.json and why rings/mol and fragment rate are reported beside it.

honest_limits: The 7-epoch arm trains on 64 clouds with 8 steps per epoch; it is a wire-in smoke, not a training result.

The epoch-0 on/off comparison is one seed. train_loss and fm_term are bit-identical, which is the claim; grad_norm differs by 1.5e-05 (2.6e-08 relative), which is float reduction noise inside the same epoch, not a flag effect.
